### prices forecast to rise in 2013, assisted by cautious recovery in global economy The accompanying table shows our forecasts for last year (given in January 2012) and actual data. as can be seen, we correctly forecasted the direction of prices, with all base metals recording a year-on-year fall in average annual prices last year. however, we underestimated the extent of the downturn. a more severe than expected slowdown in growth in the world’s largest consumer, china, was a key contributing factor which, combined with ongoing uncertainty over the health of the eurozone and the inability of the united states to promptly resolve its fiscal issues, led prices below our initial base case forecasts. The Thomson reuters Base metals index (an index of all the base metals), fell 15.1% on an average annual basis over the course of 2012. measured against this benchmark, whilst recording significant declines, copper (-9.8%), zinc (-11.2%) and lead (-14.1%), outperformed the average. meanwhile, the heavily oversupplied markets of aluminium (-15.7%) and nickel (-23.2%) underperformed, in addition to tin, which registered a 12.6% decline from a heavily inflated 2011 base. in terms of intra-year performance, and in contrast to the trends in annual average prices, the bulk of the six lme base metals (barring nickel) posted gains over the

course of last year. Perhaps logically, the largest gains on an intrayear basis were seen in the metals that emerged from 2012 with the most promising fundamentals, whilst those still burdened by oversupply were generally the laggards of the complex. The two clear outperformers last year were lead and tin, which posted gains of 15.2% and 22.1%, respectively, if we compare year-end 2012 prices to year-end 2011 levels. copper was next up, with prices gaining 4.2%. W

hilst the tightness of mine supply had been a key factor driving copper’s outperformance over previous years, more recently the market has been characterised by a gradual move to surplus and high inventory levels (within china). This, combined with the uncertain economic outlook, has served to restrict the upside for the red metal.  looking ahead, although an expected improvement in the economic environment is forecast to add upward momentum to copper prices, accelerating mine production and a move to oversupply is forecast to limit the extent of any upside. 

Finally, aluminium and nickel were the laggards of the complex.  The former did, nevertheless, close 2012 higher than it ended 2011, by 2.3%, as prices (and, in particular physical premiums) were buoyed by the fact that a large proportion of the existing inventory was, and remains, tied up in warehousing deals.  meanwhile, nickel was the only metal to record an intra-year price fall, of 9.2%, impacted by weak stainless demand and ongoing oversupply.  With both markets carrying high inventory levels into 2013, and with each expected to continue to post market surpluses this year, they remain our least favoured metals.

The chinese indicator improved to 99.7, from 99.5 in the previous month, whilst the us measure increased from 100.8 to 101.0 in the corresponding period.  Performance amongst the emerging markets of Brazil, india and russia was mixed; the Brazilian measure remained at 99.3 for the third consecutive month, that for india ticked up for the second month in a row to 97.9, whilst the russian indicator continued its downward slide to 98.6. 

Whilst us lawmakers recently struck a deal to avoid the automatic introduction of potentially devastating tax increases and spending cuts, key decisions on how to deal with the latter were delayed, rather than resolved, and will need to be revisited later in the first quarter.  The debt ceiling will also need to be addressed, with the current budget running out on 27th march.  Given such ongoing uncertainty, confidence may remain sluggish over the coming months, after crashing to a four-month low of 65.1 in December. 

Third quarter us GDP was revised up once more, with the third estimate showing growth of 3.1% (up from the second reading of 2.7%), and notably higher than the second quarter figure of 1.2%.  more recently, the ism manufacturing Pmi returned above the expansionary threshold in December, albeit only marginally at 50.7, after falling to 49.5 in November.  meanwhile, industrial production rose 0.3% in December. 

in the eurozone, there have been some pockets of positive data, such as the aforementioned oecD leading indicator for November and, more recently, an uptick in business and consumer confidence in December to 87.0, from 85.7 in November.  Nevertheless, underlying activity remains weak. eu industrial production slid on a month-on-month basis for the third consecutive month in November, by 0.3%, and on a year-on-year basis the decline was even more severe, at 3.7%, which represented the thirteenth consecutive month of contraction.  meanwhile, the eurozone manufacturing Pmi remained heavily in contractionary territory at 46.1 in December, from 46.2 in the previous month. 

recently-released chinese data confirmed both the improvement in conditions there in the fourth quarter of last year, as well as the slowdown in full year 2012 growth. real GDP growth accelerated to 7.9% year-on-year in the final three months of last year, up from 7.4% in the previous quarter.  Notwithstanding this, for the full year 2012, the economy grew 7.8%, the slowest rate of growth since 1999. 

industrial production also trended higher over the closing months of last year, with the December reading of 10.3% up from 10.1% in November, representing the fourth consecutive month of accelerating growth.  The chinese manufacturing Pmi for December also continued to show improvement, to 51.5, from 50.5 in November.  meanwhile fixed asset investment grew 20.6% on a

cumulative basis in 2012. ### ALUMINIUM ###### recent developments ###### outlook for the next twelve months **•** **_Depending on the method of measurement, aluminium prices either resisted downward pressures, or succumbed to overwhelming negative macro and fundamental factors. On an intra-year basis, aluminium ended 2012 up 2.3% compared to the close of 2011, at $2,041/tonne. However, on an annual average basis, the cash aluminium price was down 15.7% on the previous year, at $2,018/tonne. Another year of surplus and growing global production kept pressure on the metal’s price, even though stock financing activity mitigated some of the impact._** **•** **_Stocks of aluminium held in LME warehouses ended 2012 at 5.210 million tonnes, having hit a new record high on December 20th of almost 5.242 million tonnes. However, the most notable change over the last month was the surge in cancelled inventory in Detroit and Vlissingen. Shanghai exchange stocks ended 2012 up by 234,329 tonnes and stocks of primary aluminium at major Japanese ports built up by 36,700 tonnes over the year, to reach their highest level since April 2009. Meanwhile, data from the International Aluminium Institute (IAI) showed a 163,000 tonne drop in unwrought producer inventories over the whole eleven months._** **•** **_Aluminium prices turned higher at the start of the year, as relief that a drop off the fiscal cliff had seemingly been avoided pervaded through the markets. Positive Chinese data indicators have also lent support, although a rise in inflation has somewhat tempered expectations for further stimulus measures. Ongoing concerns over European and global growth have helped prices to ease back from their highs._** **•** **_We foresee another year of surplus (of 456,000 tonnes) in 2013, and we are not expecting aluminium prices to have much upside potential. However, in line with a

higher base metals complex overall, and given support from further anticipated quantitative easing in a number of countries (Japan has already announced its measures), the environment should help all metals in general._** **•** **_We also see cost pressures continuing to threaten marginal capacity throughout the year, further underpinning prices. Thomson Reuters GFMS currently forecasts a first quarter average price of $2,125 this year, with an annual average for 2013 of $2,069/tonne._** **•** **_Automotive production was positive in China and the US last year. However, European markets remain in the doldrums, with many major-producing countries recording double-digit declines; the UK bucked the trend. ###### market background aluminium ended 2012 up 2.3% compared to the close of 2011, at $2,041/tonne. however, on an annual average basis, the cash aluminium price was down 15.7% on the previous year, at $2,018/tonne. another year of surplus and growing global production kept pressure on the metal’s price, even though stock financing activity mitigated some of the impact. also, the proximity of aluminium prices to the global cost of production added a degree of support too, threatening some more marginal plants and producers. this is likely to remain the case in 2013. one thing that was apparent, however, and which we commented on several times over last year, was the

relative lack of actual production curtailments, especially to the extent needed to alleviate the global oversupply. In china, in particular, more favourable power tariffs in some regions kept threatened smelters going and we are likely to see continued net additions to capacity over the coming year. ###### cancelled lme stocks surge in december stocks of aluminium held in lme warehouses ended 2012 at 5.210 million tonnes, just below the all-time record high recorded on december 20th of almost 5.242 million tonnes and 231,600 tonnes up over the whole year. they were reported at 5.192 million at the time of writing. however, the most notable change over the last month has been to the level and proportion of cancelled inventory. unsurprisingly, the action has been focused in detroit and vlissingen, the main battlefields of the aluminium “warehouse wars”. since our last report on december 17th, while total global lme stocks have increased by 24,000 tonnes, those in detroit and vlissingen gained around 36,000 and 41,000 tonnes each, respectively. furthermore, and significantly adding to the already long off-take queues, the total increase in cancelled warrants of about 472,000 tonnes over the same period was completely accounted for by these two locations. detroit’s weekly chanGe In lme stocks vs spot prIce 150000 2200
